blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Recent advances in speech language models have improved automatic speech recognition (ASR) for long-form audio.
However, accurately and consistently transcribing domain-specific terminology remains challenging.
Motivated by the world knowledge and contextual capability of large language models (LLMs), we propose Agentic-GER, an LLM-based agent for terminology correction in long-form speech.
The agent uses global context from the full transcript to identify suspicious terms and resolve ambiguous hypotheses.
It selectively re-transcribes the source speech to check candidate corrections, and uses accepted edits to guide subsequent decisions.
Experiments with four LLMs and two ASR systems on GigaSpeechBench show consistent terminology improvements in both Chinese and English, with and without thinking.
On Chinese speech, Agentic-GER achieves up to a 36.8% relative reduction in biased character error rate (B-CER) over the Whisper baseline.
blocks.zh:
语音模式最近的进步改善了长式音频的自动语音识别(ASR).
然而,准确和一致地转录特定域的术语仍然是挑战。
受世界知识和大语言模型的背景能力驱动,我们提议使用基于LLM的Agentic-GER,在长式语音中进行术语校正。
特工利用全文中的全球背景来识别可疑术语,并解决模棱两可的假设.
它有选择地重写源词以检查候选更正,并使用被接受的编辑来指导后续的决定.
在GigaSpeech Bench上的4个LLMs和2个ASR系统的实验显示,无论在中文还是英文方面,无论有无思维,术语都有一致的改进。
在汉语语音上,Agentic-GER比Whisper基线的偏差字符误差率(B-CER)相对降低36.8%.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) has made progress in recent years [ 9 , 10 , 1 ] . Nevertheless, reliably transcribing long-form audio spanning minutes or hours remains challenging [ 14 ] . A primary bottleneck is the accurate and consistent transcription of domain-specific terminology. In lengthy recordings, rare or specialized terms are susceptible to acoustic confusion and contextual dilution, leading to inconsistent hypotheses across different segments of the same audio.
blocks.zh: 自动语音识别(ASR)近年来有所进展[9,10,1]. 然而,可靠地转录跨越数分钟或数小时的长式音频仍然具有挑战性。 主要瓶颈是域特定术语的准确和一致的转录。 在冗长的录音中,稀有或专门术语容易发生声学混淆和上下文稀释,导致同一音频不同部分的假说不一致.

blocks.en: Generative error correction (GER) uses the world knowledge and contextual capabilities of large language models (LLMs) to revise hypotheses without modifying the ASR model. Early approaches use textual evidence such as N-best lists [ 2 , 13 ] ; later work incorporates source speech [ 5 ] , retrieved entities, and contextual memory [ 3 , 7 ] .
blocks.zh: 基因错误校正(GER)使用大语言模型(LLMs)的世界知识和上下文能力来修改假说而不修改ASR模型. 早期方法使用N-best列表[2,13]等文字证据;后期工作包括源语音[5],检索的实体,以及上下文内存[3,7].

blocks.en:
Despite these advancements, applying such methods to hours-long audio requires bridging error discovery with correction.
This involves deciding which segments to re-transcribe and using context from the full transcript to resolve ambiguous ASR hypotheses.
LLM agents [ 15 ] can call tools to inspect selected audio segments while using the full transcript as context.
blocks.zh:
尽管取得了这些进步,将这种方法应用于长达数小时的音频需要通过校正发现桥接错误。
这涉及决定哪些部分要重新整理,并利用完整记录中的内容来解决模糊的ASR假设。
LLM代理[15]可以调用工具来检查选定的音频段,同时使用完整的记录稿作为上下文.

blocks.en: We view long-form correction as selective evidence acquisition guided by the full transcript. The transcript reveals recurring entities, related concepts, and cross-segment inconsistencies that indicate which parts of the source speech to inspect. This global context also constrains the candidate terms supplied by the LLM.
blocks.zh: 我们认为,长式更正是以完整记录为指南的选择性证据获取。 记录揭示了反复出现的实体、相关概念和交叉部分的不一致之处,这些不一致之处表明要检查源语言的哪些部分。 这一全球背景也限制了LLM提供的候选条件.

blocks.en: Based on this insight, we propose Agentic-GER. 1 1 1 Code: https://github.com/QwenAudio/FunResearch . As shown in Figure 1 , it scans the full transcript for suspicious spans, selectively re-transcribes the corresponding audio segments, and evaluates candidate edits using the resulting hypotheses and global context. Accepted edits update the transcript for subsequent rounds, allowing recovered terminology to inform later decisions.
blocks.zh: 基于这一见解,我们提议Agentic-GER. 11 代码:https://github.com/QuenAudio/FunResearch. 如图1所示,它扫描了可疑跨度的完整记录,有选择地重新记录了相应的音频部分,并使用由此产生的假设和全局背景来评价候选编辑. 接受编辑后为以后各轮更新记录誊本,允许恢复的术语为以后的决定提供参考.

blocks.en: We evaluate Agentic-GER on GigaSpeechBench [ 12 ] across four LLMs, two languages, and two initial ASR systems, with and without thinking. We measure terminology recognition using biased character error rate (B-CER) for Chinese and biased word error rate (B-WER) for English, which focus on annotated terminology in the reference transcripts. Agentic-GER consistently lowers these error rates in all 32 configurations, with larger gains in Chinese than in English. With Whisper, the relative B-CER reduction reaches 36.8% on Chinese speech.
blocks.zh: 我们评价GigaSpeech Bench上的 Agentic-GER [12] 跨越四个LLMs,两种语言,以及两个初始的ASR系统,无论是否思考. 我们用偏颇的汉语字符错误率(B-CER)和偏颇的英文字错误率(B-WER)来测量术语识别,这些词语侧重于参考语录中的注解术语. Agentic-GER在所有32个配置中始终降低这些错误率,中文的增益大于英文. 随着Whisper,相对的B-CER减幅在中文语音上达到36.8%.

blocks.en:
On FunASR transcripts for Chinese speech, a comparison with local GER using Qwen3.8-27B supports the value of global context: Agentic-GER improves both terminology and overall accuracy, whereas local GER trades small terminology gains for higher overall error rates.
Thinking consistently improves the 27B/31B correctors but provides limited or negative gains for Flash and Max.
blocks.zh:
在FunASR的中文语音记录上,与使用Qune3.8-27B的本地GER的比较支持了全局背景的价值:Agentic-GER既改善了术语,也提高了整体准确性,而本地GER交易的是提高整体误差率的小额术语收益.
思考一致地改进了27B/31B的校正,但为Flash和Max提供了有限的或负的收益.

blocks.en: 2.1 Error Discovery via Global Context
blocks.zh: 2.1 通过全球背景发现错误

blocks.en:
The topic of the speech narrows the set of plausible terms. Motivated by contextual
prompting [ 11 , 8 ] , the agent first extracts the topic, domain, and terms from the initial
transcript. This summary remains fixed, supplying domain cues and observed term
forms.

blocks.en:
Next, the agent uses this context to find recognition errors that may be
unremarkable within a single segment. It examines the summary, current
full transcript, and a working memory of earlier decisions, proposing
up to k k suspicious spans per round.
Each proposal specifies a segment, a short substring, and a reason for
inspection. Typical cues include inconsistent spellings of the same entity, phonetic confusions, and common words appearing in unlikely technical contexts. The proposed alternatives are evaluated in the next step.

blocks.en: 2.2 Re-transcription and Evaluation
blocks.zh: 2.2 重新招标和评价

blocks.en:
A term that fits the topic may differ from what was spoken.
For each proposed segment, the agent extracts A [ s i : e i ] A[s_{i}:e_{i}] and
re-transcribes it to obtain a second hypothesis.

blocks.en:
Finally, the agent decides whether to retain or revise each span. It
receives the current segment, its re-transcription, the candidate–evidence pairs, and the global context. The prompt asks the LLM
to assess pronunciation compatibility and support from the re-transcription
or consistent mentions elsewhere. When the re-transcription remains
ambiguous, global context can help resolve it.
The prompt requests a minimal edit, preserving unrelated words and
retaining the original if evidence is insufficient. The output contains
a keep/edit decision, the resulting segment, and a short explanation.
Figure 2 illustrates how global context helps resolve an
ambiguous re-transcription.

blocks.en: 2.3 Iterative Correction
blocks.zh: 2.3 惯性校正

blocks.en:
Recovering one occurrence makes that term available when examining other
mentions. After all candidates in a round have been evaluated using the
same transcript, the agent applies the accepted changes. Working
memory records both edits and keep decisions, including the checked spans
and their explanations. The next round uses this memory and the updated
transcript. The loop ends when no new candidates are found or the limit
on rounds or accepted edits is reached.

blocks.en: 3 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 3 实验设置

blocks.en:
We evaluate on GigaSpeechBench, using 524 Chinese
and 387 English audio files, totaling approximately 120 hours per language
across 12 domains. Initial
transcripts come from FunASR-Realtime [ 1 ] and
Whisper-Large-v3 [ 9 ] . The four LLMs are
Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma4-31B, Qwen3.8-Flash, and Qwen3.8-Max, each evaluated w/o Thinking and w/ Thinking . Thinking denotes
intermediate token generation before the task output. This yields 32 configurations.
Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma4-31B are dense models, whereas Flash and Max
are mixture-of-experts (MoE) models with 125B and 2.4T backbone
parameters, activating 6B and 95B parameters per token, respectively.
All configurations use Qwen3-ASR-1.7B [ 10 ] for segment re-transcription, without task-specific fine-tuning.
Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma4-31B, and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B are served
via vLLM on a server with four NVIDIA H100
GPUs. Flash and Max are accessed through the Alibaba Cloud Bailian API.
We set k = 4 k=4 for Chinese and k = 8 k=8 for English, with at most 32
rounds and 48 accepted edits per audio file in all configurations.

blocks.en: 4.1 Recovering Domain Terminology
blocks.zh: 4.1 收回域名术语

blocks.en:
Table 1 reports results without
thinking. Agentic-GER improves B-CER/B-WER for every evaluated
LLM under both ASR systems. The larger Flash and Max models generally
yield greater terminology gains than the 27B/31B models, with Max

On Chinese speech, Max reduces B-CER for

FunASR, whose baseline terminology error rates are lower. This shows

both ASR systems, motivating a closer look at the errors being corrected.

blocks.en: 4.3 The Value of Global Context
blocks.zh: 4.3 (中文(简体) ). 全球背景的价值

blocks.en:

local GER using Qwen3.8-27B on FunASR transcripts for Chinese speech.
Local GER corrects each segment in a single step from its original
text and the Qwen3-ASR hypothesis, without global context or
iterative updates. Table 3 reports both thinking modes.

Local GER yields small terminology gains but increases overall CER,
whereas Agentic-GER reduces both metrics. With thinking, the relative
B-CER reductions are 2.57% for local GER and
17.27% for Agentic-GER. A second ASR hypothesis
can help recover a term, but may contain errors, as
Figure 2 illustrates. Global context provides
constraints for choosing a replacement. The contrast between the two
workflows supports using the full transcript to select suspicious spans
and judge replacements across iterations, improving terminology and overall accuracy.

blocks.en: 4.4 Thinking for Terminology Recovery
blocks.zh: 4.4 对术语的思考

blocks.en:
We next examine whether thinking improves correction over the results
in Table 1 . Table 4 reports error rates
with thinking and Δ \Delta Thinking, the change in relative error
reduction in percentage points. Thinking improves Qwen3.8-27B and
Gemma4-31B in all four ASR/language combinations. Flash shows small
gains in three comparisons, whereas Max regresses in three. For Whisper
on Chinese speech, thinking increases the relative B-CER reduction by
8.5 percentage points for Qwen3.8-27B but decreases it by 9.7 points
for Max.

blocks.en:
We hypothesize that this pattern reflects a tradeoff between eliciting
relevant terminology and introducing competing alternatives.
Kambhampati et al. [ 6 ] interpret
intermediate tokens as learned prompt augmentations. For Qwen3.8-27B
and Gemma4-31B, this augmentation may help bring relevant terms into
context and connect them to the speech. Max already performs best
without thinking, suggesting less need for additional elicitation.
Further generation may introduce alternatives to a suitable correction. This interpretation is consistent with the
association between incorrect answers and increased backtracking
reported by
Hassid et al. [ 4 ] on reasoning benchmarks.

blocks.en:
Beyond its effect on accuracy, thinking also increases correction time,
with a much larger rise in output-token usage than in input-token usage.
For example, on Whisper transcripts for Chinese speech, Gemma4-31B uses
161 million input tokens and 2.6 million output tokens without thinking,
with a correction RTF of 0.42. With thinking, input usage rises to
198 million tokens and output usage to 38.3 million, while RTF reaches 5.71.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented Agentic-GER, which uses global context to guide terminology
correction in long-form speech. The full transcript helps the agent locate
suspicious spans and judge candidate replacements together with ASR
re-transcriptions. Accepted edits update the transcript, allowing recovered
terms to inform subsequent decisions. Experiments on GigaSpeechBench show
terminology improvements across all 32 configurations. Substitution
reductions contribute most to these gains, while deletions show smaller
improvements. Thinking consistently benefits the 27B/31B models but yields
limited or negative gains for Flash and Max.

blocks.en:
A promising direction is to expand the agent’s tool set. Web search could
provide domain knowledge about unfamiliar terms, while end-to-end
multimodal models could assess candidate corrections directly from speech
and transcript context. Future work will also investigate the recovery of
omitted terminology and evaluate the framework on additional datasets.

一个很有希望的方向是扩大代理工具集。 网络搜索可以
提供不熟悉术语的域知识,而端到端
多式联运模式可直接从演讲中评估候选更正
和记录上下文。 未来工作还将调查恢复
省略术语,并评价关于额外数据集的框架。
